title: Renal Colic: ED Analgesia and Imaging

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult, pregnant woman or child with suspected renal colic in the emergency department (ED): NSAID-first analgesia, imaging with low-dose non-contrast computed tomography (CT) or ultrasound, medical expulsive therapy and timing of surgery, using NICE NG118 and a randomised-trial summary. Medicine-pathway restructure on 2026-10-18: medicines regrouped into branches, steps and give-all vs choose-one options; no dose, source or clinical claim was re-checked.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.

Medicine list restructured into a branched decision pathway on 2026-10-18. Doses, routes, adjustments, monitoring, contraindications and sources are unchanged from authoring-standard-2026-10-18-tier4a-v1-live.
unverifiedSections: NICE NG118 gives no doses; the diclofenac 75 mg intramuscular, intravenous paracetamol 1 g and morphine 0.1 mg/kg intravenous doses come from a single-trial summary (Pathan et al, Lancet 2016) via a POEM page, not a guideline.

Alpha-blocker doses, antiemetic advice, infected obstructed kidney criteria, admission criteria and discharge advice were not found in the sources opened (a local ED handbook page was password-protected).
NSAID contraindications and renal function thresholds are not stated in the sources opened.
No Saudi urology guideline was opened.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

Medicine pathway: branch entry criteria, preferred options and “use when” conditions were assigned from this topic's own indications and management steps. Confirm each against the cited guideline before clinical use.

pathophysiology.summary: NICE offers an NSAID by any route as first-line treatment, intravenous paracetamol second line and opioids third line. Antispasmodics are not offered. Low-dose non-contrast CT within 24 hours is the imaging of choice in adults; ultrasound is used in pregnancy and as first-line in children. Alpha blockers are considered for distal ureteric stones under 10 mm (off-label as of January 2019).

clinicalManagement.title: Analgesia
actions: Offer an NSAID by any route first (trial: diclofenac 75 mg intramuscularly); intravenous paracetamol 1 g if NSAIDs are contraindicated or insufficient; opioids only if both fail (trial: morphine 0.1 mg/kg intravenously).

clinicalManagement.title: Imaging
actions: Adults: low-dose non-contrast CT. Pregnancy: ultrasound instead. Children: ultrasound first, then low-dose CT if unclear.

clinicalManagement.title: Medical expulsive therapy
actions: Consider an alpha blocker for distal ureteric stones under 10 mm (off-label).

clinicalManagement.title: Definitive treatment
actions: Offer surgical treatment within 48 hours if pain is ongoing and not tolerated or the stone is unlikely to pass.

clinicalManagement.title: Children
actions: Consider referral to a paediatric nephrologist or urologist for assessment and metabolic investigations.
